A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Text2VDM and retain matching core experiments. Text, equations, tables and figures are readable. The comparison includes v2's Appendices A–C; the supplied v1 ends with references.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original generation experiments, ablations, a 40-prompt quantitative evaluation and a 32-participant user study.

after.justification: Section 4 retains these original empirical results and adds diagnostic comparisons and supplementary qualitative results.

M1.justification: The initialization, masking, rendering and Compel blending components remain. However, Equation (3) revises the stated optimization step from updating v* with (I - λL)^-1 to updating v with (I + λL)^-1. This changes the documented procedure; the PDFs do not establish whether the implementation changed.

E1.justification: v2 adds an auxiliary 2D text-to-image test scenario for examining semantic decoupling (Figure 8). The principal tasks remain surface-detail and geometric-structure brush generation. Appendix B.3's enumeration of 40 prompts documents existing evaluation coverage rather than establishing a new benchmark.

E2.justification: v2 evaluates SDS with Attend-and-Excite in Figure 7 and adds direct Laplacian regularization as a control in Figure 4. Paint-it, Text2Mesh and TextDeformer remain the principal comparison methods. Newly cited GenVDM is not evaluated.

E3.justification: The 40-prompt evaluation, 12 rendered evaluation views and 32-person study remain unchanged. Figure 4 replaces the λ = 45 condition with a direct-regularization control, and Figure 7 reduces the CSD weight settings from 0.1, 0.5 and 1 to 0.1 and 0.5. Newly disclosed implementation settings do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands analysis of the central design choices: preconditioning versus direct regularization, Compel versus Attend-and-Excite, and direct 2D visualization of semantic suppression and enhancement. Appendices add a surface-detail semantic-enhancement ablation, intermediate mask-guided optimization results and a beard failure comparison. The initialization ablation and part of the snail-shell analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance tests. The descriptive averaging and user-preference reporting remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 are numerically unchanged, including Text2VDM's CLIP score of 0.2556, self-intersection of 0.77%, and preference rates of 75.3% and 67.6%. Qualitative results expand substantially through the new controls, 2D diagnostics and supplementary comparisons. Some earlier outputs, including λ = 45 and CSD weight 1, are removed; these changes do not demonstrate a same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: Equation (3) changes both the preconditioner sign and the optimization variable/gradient, constituting a mathematical revision beyond notation. Equation (2) and the token-blending formula remain. The token weight is also unchanged: v2's 1.1 squared equals v1's 1.21. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a text-to-VDM framework that mitigates semantic coupling and produces reusable brushes compatible with modeling workflows. Renaming CFG-weighted SDS as Semantic Enhancement SDS does not materially change these core contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds an explanation linking Attend-and-Excite instability to changing camera poses and noise, contrasting this with fixed Compel embeddings. It also discusses the mask-alignment/diversity tradeoff and adds inherited T2I anatomical errors, such as incorrect finger counts, to the retained multiview-consistency limitation.

D1.justification: Appendices A–B supply substantial previously absent reproducibility information: Stable Diffusion 2.1, camera distributions, four views per iteration, 10,000 iterations, RTX 4090 hardware, approximately 40 minutes per brush, EXR baking, Paint-it adaptation details, and all 40 prompts with initialization/mask assignments. These are disclosures rather than evidence that existing experiments changed.

R1.justification: v2 adds positioning against concurrent, image-conditioned GenVDM, introduces Attend-and-Excite into the discussion, and cites two procedural-material studies. The broader relationship to existing 3D editing and brush-generation research remains intact.

P1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.3 and 4.3 undergo substantial rewriting and reorganization around Sobolev preconditioning and semantic enhancement. Terminology changes throughout, related-work headings are reformatted, and application discussion is redistributed into structured Appendices A–C. These changes extend beyond inserting new results.

P2.justification: v2 revises the method diagram and several comparison/ablation panels, adds the 2D diagnostic, interface and initialization illustrations, introduces a prompt table, and expands the visual result galleries. Some displays are relocated rather than new: notably, v1's pillar example in Figure 10 becomes v2 Figure 19.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses substantial reproducibility gaps by documenting the model, camera sampling, optimization budget, prompts and baseline setup, while new controls better support its central design choices. These gains improve auditability and scientific support despite unchanged quantitative scores. A remaining flaw is that Section 4.1 claims shared initialization and masks for all methods, whereas Appendix B.2 exempts Paint-it; this inconsistency does not outweigh the substantial documentation and analytical improvements.
